Checklist Item: UI layout matches approved design mockups/Figma files for all page templates at desktop and mobile viewports
Spacing and padding between elements matches design specifications within acceptable tolerance (2-4px)
Visual alignment of elements (text baseline alignment; icon-to-text alignment; grid column alignment) matches design intent
Font weights and styles render correctly across all browsers and match design specifications
Text truncation and overflow behavior (ellipsis; line clamping; wrapping) is intentional and consistent across components
Line height and letter spacing produce comfortable reading experience for body text and headings
Brand colors are applied consistently across all pages and components; no off-brand color variants visible
Image style and quality are consistent with brand guidelines (photography style; illustration style; icon set)
Placeholder and stock images replaced with final brand-approved assets before production
Icon style is consistent throughout the application (outline vs filled; stroke width; size proportions)
Icon strategy reviewed and consistent (font icons vs SVG inline vs SVG sprite); chosen approach appropriate for project requirements
Visual hierarchy clearly guides user attention to primary actions and content on each page
White space usage creates clear content groupings and avoids cluttered appearance
Interactive element states (hover; active; disabled; selected) are visually distinct and consistent across all components
Disabled state styling clearly communicates non-interactivity without reducing readability below WCAG contrast thresholds
Navigation structure is logical and discoverable; users can reach any page within 3 clicks from homepage
Breadcrumb trails are accurate and update correctly during navigation; breadcrumbs reflect actual page hierarchy
Back button behavior is predictable; browser history entries match user expectations for each navigation action
Deep linking and URL sharing work correctly; shared URLs render the expected page state
Core user flows (signup; login; purchase; search) are intuitive and require minimal steps to complete
Multi-step processes (wizards; checkout flows) show clear progress indication and allow backward navigation
Destructive actions (delete; cancel; overwrite) require explicit confirmation with clear consequences explained
Loading states provide appropriate visual feedback (spinners; skeleton screens; progress bars) for operations >300ms
Skeleton screens and shimmer effects match the general shape of final content layout
Empty states (no results; no data; first-time use) have meaningful content with guidance on next steps
Error recovery paths are clear; users can easily return to a working state after encountering an error
Success and failure feedback is timely and visible without requiring user to scroll or search for confirmation
Toast notifications and banners auto-dismiss after appropriate duration and do not obscure critical content
Form validation messaging is clear and specific; tells user exactly what is wrong and how to fix it
Inline validation timing is appropriate (on blur for most fields; debounced for search/username availability)
Form field order follows logical data entry sequence; tab order matches visual layout
Auto-fill and password manager compatibility verified for login and registration forms
Long forms are broken into logical sections or steps with clear section headings
Animations and transitions enhance understanding of state changes without feeling excessive or distracting
Page transitions feel smooth and responsive; no jarring jumps or flashes between views
Content is free of spelling and grammatical errors across all pages and components
Microcopy (button labels; tooltips; placeholders; helper text) is clear and consistent in tone and terminology
Technical jargon avoided in user-facing text; language appropriate for target audience reading level
Content hierarchy guides users through information logically; most important information first
Legal and compliance text (terms of service; privacy policy; disclaimers) is present where required and links are functional
Cookie consent banner meets regional compliance requirements (GDPR; CCPA; ePrivacy); consent choices are respected across sessions
Privacy policy and terms of service links are accessible from all pages (typically in footer)
User data handling and storage practices comply with applicable privacy regulations
Visual appearance consistent across target browsers (Chrome; Firefox; Safari; Edge) at common viewport sizes
Web fonts render consistently across browsers; no FOIT (Flash of Invisible Text) or excessive FOUT (Flash of Unstyled Text)
CSS animations and transitions perform smoothly across all target browsers without visual glitches
JavaScript-dependent features work correctly across all target browsers including Safari and Firefox
Touch interactions work correctly on iOS and Android devices; no double-tap-to-zoom interference with button clicks
Touch target sizes are adequate for finger interaction (minimum 44x44px perceived area per WCAG 2.5.8)
Swipe gestures (where implemented) work reliably and do not conflict with browser navigation gestures
Scrolling behavior is smooth on mobile devices; no scroll jank or rubber-banding issues on content areas
Landscape and portrait orientations handled gracefully; layout adapts without content clipping or overflow
Mobile keyboard does not obscure active input field; page scrolls to keep focused input visible
Appropriate mobile keyboard types triggered for different input fields (numeric for phone; email keyboard for email; URL keyboard for web addresses)
Layout adapts gracefully at all viewport widths; no awkward intermediate states between defined breakpoints
Content reflow between breakpoints maintains logical reading order and visual hierarchy
Images scale appropriately without distortion or pixelation across all viewport sizes
Typography remains readable at all viewport sizes; no text too small to read on mobile or oversized on desktop
Tables are usable on mobile viewports (horizontal scroll; responsive table pattern; or reformatted layout)
Navigation adapts appropriately for mobile (hamburger menu; bottom navigation; or collapsed navigation pattern)
Mobile navigation overlay does not create accessibility issues; can be closed easily; does not trap focus unexpectedly
Screen reader announces page content in logical and meaningful order matching visual hierarchy
Custom interactive components (dropdowns; tabs; accordions; carousels) are understandable and operable via screen reader
Dynamic content changes (loaded results; updated counts; live regions) are announced appropriately by screen reader
Image alt text accurately conveys meaning and context of images; decorative images properly hidden from screen reader
Cognitive load is appropriate for target audience; complex processes broken into manageable steps
Instructions do not rely solely on sensory characteristics (shape; color; size; position) to convey information
Consistent and predictable interaction patterns used throughout the application; no unexpected behaviors
Time-based content and session timeouts provide adequate warnings and options to extend
Color choices reviewed for accessibility with color vision deficiency simulators (protanopia; deuteranopia; tritanopia)
Information conveyed by color is also conveyed through text labels; patterns; or icons
Content remains functional and readable at 400% zoom as required by WCAG 2.1 AA Reflow criterion
Interactive elements have visible text labels or accessible names that voice control users can speak to activate
Page is usable via switch access navigation; interactive elements reachable in reasonable number of switch activations
Above-the-fold content loads and renders within perceptually acceptable time (<2.5s) on representative network conditions
Page transitions and route changes feel responsive; no visible white flashes or layout jumps during navigation
Scroll performance is smooth with no visible jank on content-heavy pages and list views
Large datasets presented with appropriate pagination or virtualization; no perceptible lag during scrolling
Offline or slow network experience degrades gracefully; appropriate fallback UI shown when resources fail to load
Third-party script failures (analytics; chat widgets; social embeds) do not block or degrade core page functionality
RTL (right-to-left) layout renders correctly for RTL languages; mirrored layout is complete including icons and directional elements
Text expansion (translations up to 200% longer than English) does not break layouts or cause overflow/truncation
Date; time; number; and currency formats match target locale conventions and user preferences
Currency symbols and decimal separators correct for target markets
Translated content fits within UI containers without clipping; buttons and labels accommodate longer translations
Cultural sensitivity reviewed for images; icons; color meanings; and metaphors across target markets
AEM or CMS-specific frontend build tooling (ui.frontend; clientlib pipeline) configured correctly for the platform version
Webfont loading strategy reviewed; font-display behavior prevents Flash of Invisible Text (FOIT) in production
Third-party library and framework choices are justified; no redundant libraries serving the same purpose
jQuery usage patterns reviewed for performance (selectors are performant; jQuery objects are cached; event delegation used where appropriate)
Feature detection strategy reviewed (Modernizr or native feature detection) for progressive enhancement where legacy browser support required
CSS architecture follows agreed methodology (BEM; ITCSS; utility-first) consistently across all components
Atomic and reusable CSS utility classes created for common patterns (spacing; typography; colors) to reduce duplication
Component CSS is self-contained and does not create unintended side effects on sibling or parent elements
Component library documentation is complete; up to date; and includes usage examples for each component variant
Design system tokens in code match latest design specifications; no drift between design tool and implementation
Functions and complex code blocks have descriptive comments explaining purpose and business logic rationale
JSDoc or equivalent documentation present for public API functions and component props
Component prop interfaces are well-defined; use specific types (not 'any'); and documented with descriptions
Structured data (JSON-LD / Schema.org) is valid; complete; and relevant to page content type
Google Rich Results Test passes for all structured data markup on key page templates
Open Graph meta tags (og:title; og:description; og:image; og:url) present and correct on shareable pages
Twitter Card meta tags present; shared links preview correctly on social media platforms
Sitemap.xml is complete; up to date; and submitted to search engines; all important pages included
Robots.txt is configured correctly; does not inadvertently block important pages or assets from crawling
Internal linking strategy promotes content discoverability; orphan pages (no internal links pointing to them) identified and addressed
Project management tool (Jira; Azure DevOps; Linear; Asana; or equivalent) is set up and actively used; all active work tracked as tickets/issues with status updates
Jira/issue board reflects current sprint or iteration work accurately; no stale tickets in 'In Progress' beyond sprint duration; backlog is groomed and prioritized
Tickets/issues have clear acceptance criteria; description; priority; and assignee before moving to development; Definition of Ready criteria followed
Bug tickets include reproduction steps; expected vs actual behavior; environment details; and severity classification
Git commits and pull requests reference Jira/issue ticket IDs; work is traceable from requirement to code change to deployment
Definition of Done (DoD) is documented and agreed upon by the team; includes criteria for code review; testing; accessibility; and documentation
Design tool (Figma; Sketch; Adobe XD; or equivalent) is used for all UI design work; design files are organized and accessible to the development team
Figma (or equivalent) component library mirrors the development component library; design tokens (colors; spacing; typography) are synchronized between design and code
Design files include specifications for all viewport breakpoints (mobile; tablet; desktop); not just desktop-only mockups
Design-to-development handoff process is defined; includes design review meeting; specification walkthrough; and asset export standards
Design QA step exists in workflow; designer reviews implemented UI against original designs before ticket is marked complete
Interactive prototypes or user flow diagrams provided for complex interactions (multi-step forms; animations; state transitions) before development begins
Branching strategy is documented (Git Flow; GitHub Flow; Trunk-Based Development; or custom) and understood by all team members
Release branch or tag strategy is defined; releases are versioned (semantic versioning preferred); release process is documented and repeatable
Hotfix process is documented; emergency fixes can be deployed without disrupting ongoing feature development; hotfix branches merge back to both main and develop
Feature branches are short-lived (merged within 1-2 sprints); long-running branches reviewed for integration risk and merge conflict potential
Code review checklist or guidelines documented; reviewers check for functionality; readability; security; performance; and accessibility during review
Code reviews completed within agreed SLA (e.g. 24 hours for standard PRs; 4 hours for hotfixes); no PRs stale in review for >3 business days
Code review feedback is constructive and specific; review comments reference coding standards or best practices where applicable
Pair programming or mob programming practiced for complex features or critical bug fixes; knowledge shared across team members
QA testing process defined; includes functional testing; regression testing; and exploratory testing phases before release
QA environment(s) available that mirror production configuration; QA testing not performed directly on production
Regression test suite maintained and executed before each release; test cases updated when features change
Cross-browser and cross-device testing matrix defined; target browsers/devices documented and tested before each major release
Accessibility testing included in QA process; screen reader testing performed on critical user flows before release (NVDA/JAWS on Windows; VoiceOver on macOS/iOS; TalkBack on Android)
UAT (User Acceptance Testing) or stakeholder sign-off required before production deployment; sign-off criteria documented
Release checklist documented and followed for each deployment; includes pre-deployment checks; deployment steps; and post-deployment verification
Rollback plan documented and tested; team can revert a failed deployment within defined time threshold (e.g. <15 minutes)
Production deployment notifications sent to relevant stakeholders; deployment windows communicated in advance for planned releases
Post-deployment monitoring in place (error tracking; performance monitoring; uptime checks); alerts configured for anomalies after release
Incident response process documented; team knows escalation paths; severity classification; and communication channels for production issues
Technical documentation (architecture decisions; ADRs; system diagrams) maintained and kept current as the system evolves
Onboarding documentation exists for new developers; includes local environment setup; codebase overview; coding standards; and workflow guide
Technical debt is tracked (tagged tickets in Jira; dedicated backlog column); regularly reviewed and prioritized for remediation
Knowledge sharing practices in place (tech talks; brown bags; architecture reviews; shared documentation wiki); no single points of failure for critical system knowledge
Dependency update policy documented; dependencies reviewed and updated on a regular cadence (monthly or quarterly); security patches applied within defined SLA
Third-party library evaluation criteria documented (license compatibility; maintenance status; community support; bundle size impact) before adoption
Secrets management process defined; API keys and credentials stored in vault or environment variables; no secrets shared via chat or email; secret rotation policy in place
GenAI usage policy documented and communicated to all team members; policy covers approved tools; permitted use cases; data handling restrictions; and code review requirements for AI-generated output

Approved GenAI tools list maintained (e.g. GitHub Copilot; Cursor; ChatGPT; Claude; Amazon CodeWhisperer); only licensed and organization-approved tools used; unauthorized tools not connected to codebase or repositories

GenAI tool licensing and subscription managed centrally; business/enterprise tiers used where available to ensure data privacy and IP protection; free/personal tier usage on proprietary code prohibited

Confidential or proprietary source code; customer data; and internal business logic not submitted as prompts to public GenAI services without data-privacy safeguards (enterprise plans; self-hosted models; or DLP controls)
GenAI usage compliant with client contractual obligations; client-specific restrictions on AI-assisted development reviewed and adhered to; disclosure provided where contractually required
GenAI-assisted code clearly identified in PRs (PR description notes AI tool used; or commit metadata tags AI-assisted changes); reviewers aware which sections are AI-generated for enhanced scrutiny

AI-generated code undergoes same code review rigor as human-written code; reviewers verify logic correctness; edge case handling; error scenarios; and security implications rather than rubber-stamping

GenAI tools configured with project-specific context (custom instructions; codebase-aware settings; .cursorrules; .github/copilot-instructions.md) to align output with project coding standards and conventions

AI-generated tests reviewed for meaningful assertions; tests verify actual business logic rather than trivially asserting implementation details; no AI-generated tests that always pass regardless of code behavior
GenAI tools used for code review assistance (identifying bugs; security issues; performance concerns) as supplement to human review; AI review findings validated by human reviewer before action
Developers understand the code they commit regardless of generation method; team members can explain AI-generated logic during code review or architecture discussions; no 'black box' code merged
AI-generated architecture and design pattern suggestions reviewed by senior developer or architect; GenAI not used as sole decision-maker for architectural choices without human validation
Prompt engineering best practices shared within team for common development tasks (component creation; test writing; refactoring; documentation); reusable prompt templates maintained where applicable

AI-generated documentation (README sections; JSDoc; inline comments; ADRs) reviewed for accuracy; no hallucinated feature descriptions; API references; or configuration instructions committed without verification
Regular retrospective or review of GenAI tool effectiveness; team evaluates productivity impact; code quality trends; and identifies patterns where AI assistance helps vs. introduces issues
AI-generated code reviewed for potential intellectual property concerns; no substantial verbatim reproduction of third-party copyrighted code; legal team consulted on AI-code ownership policy
AI code generation telemetry and data-sharing settings reviewed; opt-out of code snippet sharing where available; AI tool data retention policies reviewed and acceptable for project classification

AI-generated UI components reviewed for accessibility compliance; GenAI tools frequently omit ARIA attributes; keyboard handlers; and semantic HTML; manual verification required for all AI-generated markup
AI-generated content (copy; alt text; error messages) reviewed for bias; inclusivity; and cultural sensitivity; no stereotypical or exclusionary language in AI-suggested text
